newsitem.title: USA: Western National to sell via the Internet. [CORRECTED 21:55 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Western National to sell via the Internet. [CORRECTED 21:55 GMT]

text.p: Western National Corp said it plans to begin using the Internet to streamline administrative processing of insurance policies with an eye toward one day selling policies over the Internet (corrects from "... plans to begin selling some of its life insurance and annuity products over the Internet sometime next year").

Western National said its Western National Life subsidiary will transact business with field agents, policyholders and other constituents over the World Wide Web through the use of a new software package called PolicyNet.
Western National Life is the first to use PolicyNet, which was developed by the Leverage Group in Glastonbury, Conn., a provider of life insurance and annuity systems for the insurance industry.
Western National will use PolicyNet in combination with the Leverage Group's PolicyLink Administration System, a local-area-network-based system policy administration system.
Western National expects PolicyLink to be in operation by late summer, with PolicyNet to follow in 1998.
"We place considerable importance on our choice of technology solutions and business partners," Western National vice chairman John Graf said in a statement.

"With PolicyNet, we will be able to transact business easily and efficiently on the Internet with our most important constituents," he said. "PolicyLink will further enhance our highly efficient administrative and customer service operations," he said.
